subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: Which owner boundary should drive the remaining healthy-local-vLLM false-timeout and gateway-latency work after the landed partial fixes?
rationale: The remaining report crosses provider timeout policy, stream watchdogs, auth-profile fallback, cron/live-session behavior, and gateway RPC availability, and current evidence does not identify one safe implementation path without maintainer intent and live proof.

options.title: Run Canonical Live Repro First
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main or current-release local vLLM trace before selecting the code owner boundary.

options.title: Promote A Narrower Canonical Tracker
options.body: If the new trace matches an open timeout/deadlock issue, move the remaining work to that exact tracker and close this one only after preserving the evidence link.

options.title: Close Only After End-To-End Proof
options.body: Treat the landed partial fixes as sufficient only if a current build no longer reproduces the false-timeout and `sessions_spawn` latency cascade.

recommendation.title: Run Canonical Live Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main or current-release local vLLM trace before selecting the code owner boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the current assignee and already made the adjacent cron fallback provider/auth decision that overlaps this issue's remaining routing semantics.
